document_text:
# Claridade – Company and Product Brief

Launch of the Lumora sunrise alarm lamp in Spain. Internal document for the launch planning team. All companies, people and figures in this document are fictional and used for evaluation only.

## 1. Company overview

Claridade Lda is a Portuguese consumer electronics company founded in 2019 in Porto by Inês Carvalho, an industrial designer, and Rui Antunes, an electronics engineer. It designs smart lighting products for the home and manufactures them through a partner factory in northern Portugal.

In 2024 Claridade had 23 employees and a turnover of 5.1 million euros, 85% in Portugal. Its products are sold in about 420 electronics and home stores in Portugal, on Amazon Portugal and through its own online shop, which accounts for 31% of sales.

## 2. The product: Lumora

Lumora is a bedside lamp that wakes the user with light that grows gradually brighter over 30 minutes, simulating a sunrise, followed by a soft sound.

- Brightness up to 300 lux; colour from deep red to daylight white.
- Sunset mode for falling asleep, 8 natural sounds, FM radio.
- App for iOS and Android; works without the app with physical buttons.
- 2-year warranty, repairable design with replaceable parts.
- Recommended retail price in Portugal: 89 euros.

In a home test run by the company in Portugal in 2024 (180 participants, 4 weeks), 64% said they woke up "more easily" than with their usual alarm, and 71% kept using the lamp after the test. The test had no control group.

Intended price in Spain: 89 to 99 euros.

## 3. Why Spain, and launch goals

Spain is Claridade's closest large market, and the company already ships online orders there. Daylight saving time and late sunrises in western Spain make winter mornings dark until about 8:30.

Goals for the Spanish launch, approved by the board in September 2025:

- Sell 40,000 units in Spain in the first 18 months.
- Be listed in at least 600 stores, including one national electronics chain.
- Reach a 4.3 rating or higher on Amazon Spain within the first year.

The launch is planned for October 2026, before the winter season.

## 4. Market context

Figures from the report "Smart home lighting in Spain 2025" by IberiaTech Insights and from the Panel Hogar 2025 consumer survey (both fictional sources for this evaluation).

| Indicator | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Wake-up light market in Spain (2024) | 21 million euros | IberiaTech Insights 2025 |
| Market growth 2022-2024 | +9% per year | IberiaTech Insights 2025 |
| Average price of a wake-up light sold in Spain | 74 euros | IberiaTech Insights 2025 |
| Adults who have difficulty waking up in winter | 38% | Panel Hogar 2025 |

Sales by channel (2024): online marketplaces 46%, electronics chains 31%, department stores 14%, other 9%.

## 5. Consumer groups

The Panel Hogar 2025 measured interest in "a sunrise alarm lamp at about 90 euros" among Spanish adults aged 18 to 64 (about 30 million people).

| Group | Adults | Share of adults 18-64 | Purchase intent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Adults who have difficulty waking up in winter | 11.4 million | 38% | 24% |
| Shift workers (early or rotating shifts) | 2.1 million | 7% | 29% |
| Parents of children under 10 | 5.3 million | 18% | 17% |
| Students living away from home | 1.2 million | 4% | 12% |

Interest is higher among women (27%) than men (19%). Price is the main reason for not buying: 46% of non-interested adults say 90 euros is too much for an alarm.

## 6. Competitors

- **Philips Wake-up Light**: market leader, sold in all electronics chains, several models from 60 to 200 euros.
- **Lumie**: British brand, premium models, mainly online.
- **Unbranded imports** on online marketplaces, from 25 euros, often with poor reviews.

Claridade has not compared features and prices in detail.

## 7. Distribution and marketing

Claridade sells online in Spain already (about 1,900 units in 2024 without marketing). It is negotiating with one national electronics chain and two department store groups. The marketing budget for the first 18 months is 450,000 euros.

## 8. Open points

- Target group and positioning.
- Price point within the 89-99 euro range.
- Launch campaign concept and channel plan.

analysis.market_overview: The Spanish wake-up light market was worth 21 million euros in 2024, grew about 9% per year in 2022-2024, and the average price is 74 euros [S3]. In 2024 sales went mainly through online marketplaces (46%), then electronics chains (31%), department stores (14%) and other channels (9%) [S3]. 38% of adults say they have difficulty waking up in winter [S3]. Philips is the market leader, sold in all electronics chains. Lumie is a premium British brand sold mainly online. Cheap unbranded imports start at 25 euros and often have poor reviews [S5]. Spanish review articles treat Philips models as the reference [S8][S9]. Lumora's intended price of 89 to 99 euros is above the 74-euro average [S1][S3]. Price is the main barrier: 46% of adults not interested in the product say 90 euros is too much [S4]. Claridade already ships online to Spain (about 1,900 units in 2024, no marketing) and has a 450,000-euro marketing budget for 18 months [S6]. The goal is 40,000 units in 18 months [S2].

competitors.name: Philips Wake-up Light (HF3531, HF3520/SmartSleep, HF3651/Somneo)
competitors.positioning: Market leader, sold in all electronics chains and the reference brand in Spanish review articles; several models. HF3531: 300 lux, 7 natural sounds, FM radio, USB phone charging, no app or WiFi control, described as bulky. HF3520 is called best value for money and HF3651 the most complete. Reported as medically certified.

competitors.name: Lumie (Bodyclock range)
competitors.positioning: British brand specialised in wake-up and light-therapy lamps; premium models, mainly online, with a presence on Amazon.es. Models include Rise 100 (fixed 30 min sunrise, beep alarm only), Glow 150 (20-45 min sunrise, 10 sounds) and Shine 300 (15-90 min sunrise, 14 sounds, FM radio). Reported as medically certified. Reviewers found the cheaper models easy to use but limited in brightness options.

competitors.name: Unbranded imports on online marketplaces
competitors.positioning: Low-cost generic sunrise alarm lights sold on marketplaces, often with poor reviews.

competitors.name: Smartia
competitors.positioning: Named 'Smartia 2025', the cheapest entry option for trying light-based waking without spending much.

competitors.name: Blonbar
competitors.positioning: Wake-up lamp listed in a Spanish ranking as 'best design'.

customer_needs: Easier, less abrupt waking in winter: 38% of adults have difficulty waking up in winter [S3]
Realistic, smooth sunrise simulation, from dim red to warm orange to bright white at about 300 lux [S7]
Convenience features such as FM radio, nature sounds and USB phone charging [S8][S15]
A sunset function to help falling asleep [S12]
Control over sunrise duration and brightness; reviewers criticised limited brightness options and having to re-enable the alarm every day [S16]
A display that dims or switches off at night, and a less bulky design [S7]
Medical certification, which is highlighted for Philips and Lumie in review coverage [S7]
An affordable price: 46% of non-interested adults say 90 euros is too much for an alarm [S4]
A cheap entry option for trying light-based waking [S9]
Trustworthy products with good reviews, given that cheap imports often have poor reviews [S5]

segments.label: Adults with difficulty waking in winter
segments.description: Spanish adults aged 18-64 who find it hard to wake up in winter. Purchase intent for a sunrise alarm lamp at about 90 euros is 24% [S4]. This is the largest group.
needs: Gentle, gradual waking on dark winter mornings
A price near 90 euros that feels justified
Proof that the lamp works (the Portuguese home test had no control group)

segments.label: Shift workers
segments.description: Adults working early or rotating shifts. They have the highest purchase intent of the four groups, at 29% [S4].
needs: Reliable waking at changing or very early times
Sunset mode and sounds to help falling asleep at irregular hours

segments.label: Parents of children under 10
segments.description: Parents of young children. Purchase intent is 17% [S4].
needs: Gentler waking in a household with early mornings
Simple use, with physical buttons as well as the app

segments.label: Students living away from home
segments.description: Students living away from their family home. They have the lowest purchase intent, at 12% [S4], and the smallest size of the four groups.

data_quality_notes: Gap: no Spanish price found for Lumora competitors that is reliable. Lumie has no Spanish price except Rise 100 at about 115 euros in one YouTube video (weak). Lumie UK prices in pounds were found and not used.

Conflict: web prices for Philips (167 euros on Amazon and 282 euros at MediaMarkt for the HF3531, 142 euros for the HF3520, Somneo HF3651 from 229.99 euros) differ from the document's 60-200 euro range. The Philips price level 'high' is therefore an assumption based on these indicative web prices and on the 74-euro market average. The Idealo snippet is partly unclear.
Price levels for Lumie ('premium') come from the document only [S5]. Smartia is 'low' only because a review calls it the cheapest option, and no price was found. Blonbar has no price.

Weak sources: Spanish review articles and YouTube videos often contain affiliate links. The 'medically certified' claim for Philips and Lumie comes from one article. Lumora has no such certification claim in the document.
The document's market figures (IberiaTech Insights 2025, Panel Hogar 2025) are described as fictional and no independent web figure for the Spanish market was found, so they could not be checked.

Segment sizes and intent are taken from the document. The document does not say whether the groups overlap, so they should not be added together. Stated intent is not actual purchase. Intent was measured for a lamp 'at about 90 euros', so intent at 99 euros is unknown.

Segment needs are inferred from the group definitions, the document and general competitor-feature evidence. No source states needs specific to shift workers, parents or students. They are weakly supported.

Derived, not from a source: 21M euros / 74 euros is about 284,000 units a year. The 21M figure is a value, not a unit count, so this is only a rough check that 40,000 units in 18 months would be a large share of the category.
The Lumora home test (180 participants, 4 weeks, Portugal, no control group; 64% woke up more easily, 71% kept using it) is weak evidence of effect and was run in Portugal, not Spain [S1].

Not verified: the document's claim that winter mornings in western Spain stay dark until about 8:30. Press on the return to winter time was found but no figures were retrieved. A Spanish government proposal to end seasonal clock changes could affect the seasonal argument; the result was ambiguous.

Gaps: no Amazon.es rating data (needed for the 4.3 goal), no competitor warranty or repairability information, no feature-and-price comparison done by Claridade, and no confirmation of Lumie's availability in Spanish stores.
Competitor feature statements for Philips HF3531 and Lumie come from review articles and retailer listings and were not checked against manufacturer specifications.

sources.reference: Company document, section 3 (Why Spain, and launch goals)

strategy.target_description: Spanish adults aged 18-64 who find it hard to wake up on dark winter mornings (11.4 million people, 38% of adults 18-64). They are mainstream buyers who want a gentler start to the day. They are willing to pay about 90 euros if the price feels justified.
strategy.positioning_statement: For Spanish adults who struggle to get up on dark winter mornings, Lumora is the smart sunrise alarm lamp that gives a full-featured, gradual 30-minute sunrise (up to 300 lux, deep red to daylight white), a sunset mode, 8 natural sounds and FM radio. It is simple to use, with the app or with physical buttons, and it is built to last, with a 2-year warranty and replaceable parts. It is positioned as a modern, easy-to-live-with alternative to the Philips reference models, at a clearly lower price than Philips' indicative web prices. It is also a more trustworthy step up from cheap unbranded imports, and it is more complete than Lumie's entry models. No medical, efficacy or "better than Philips/Lumie" claims are made.
strategy.value_proposition: A gentler wake-up on dark winter mornings, with a natural sunrise light and a soft sound. The same lamp helps you wind down in the evening with sunset mode. You get the features buyers look for (300 lux, sounds, FM radio, sunset mode) at around 90 euros. It works with or without the app and is designed to be repaired, not replaced.
strategy.pricing_direction: Launch at the bottom of the intended range, 89 euros, and do not go to 99 euros at launch. Reasons: (1) 89 euros is already above the 74-euro market average [S3]. (2) 46% of adults not interested in the product say 90 euros is too much [S4]. (3) Purchase intent of 24% was measured at "about 90 euros", and intent at 99 euros is unknown [S4]. Philips is priced higher on the indicative web prices (about 142 euros for the HF3520, 167 euros or more for the HF3531). These prices conflict with the document's range and are only indicative [S5][S15], so the "below Philips" position is an assumption. No reliable Spanish price exists for Lumie (only a weak Rise 100 figure of about 115 euros). Before fixing the final price, Claridade should compare Philips and Lumie prices and features on the Spanish market, and could test 99 euros on its own online shop. Avoid price promotions that undercut the premium over cheap imports at 25 euros and up.
strategy.rationale: SEG1 is chosen because it is the only segment large enough for the 40,000-unit goal [S2]. It has 11.4 million adults and a 24% purchase intent at about 90 euros [S4]. That implies roughly 2.7 million interested adults (derived: 11.4M x 24%; intent is not purchase, and overlap with other groups is unknown [S4]). The alternatives are weaker on size. SEG2, shift workers, has the highest intent (29%) but only 2.1 million adults, or about 0.6 million interested (derived). 40,000 units would be about 6.6% of that pool, against about 1.5% of the SEG1 pool, so SEG2 alone is too small for the goal. SEG3, parents, has 5.3 million adults and 17% intent, about 0.9 million interested (derived), which is lower in both size and interest. SEG4, students, has 1.2 million adults, 12% intent and a low-price need that does not fit an 89-99 euro product [S4]. Shift workers and parents can be reached with secondary messages (flexible alarm and sunset mode, simple physical buttons), but they are not the focus. Their needs are only weakly supported [S4]. On competition, Philips is the reference and is sold in all electronics chains [S5][S8][S9], but its HF3531 has no app or WiFi control and is described as bulky [S15][S7]. Lumie is premium and mainly online [S5]. Cheap imports have poor reviews [S5]. This leaves room for a trustworthy, full-featured option near 90 euros. On channels, marketplaces were 46% of 2024 sales, electronics chains 31% and department stores 14% [S3]. Claridade already ships to Spain online (about 1,900 units in 2024 without marketing) and has a 450,000-euro budget over 18 months [S6]. Amazon.es and the own online shop are therefore the safest starting channels. Amazon.es also matters for the 4.3 rating goal, although no rating data is available for it. The electronics chain and department stores are essential for the 600-store goal and for the 31% and 14% channel shares. However, negotiations are ongoing and no agreement is confirmed (brief), so the store goal is a risk. Product review media are included because Spanish review articles treat Philips as the reference [S8][S9], and getting Lumora into those reviews is how it can enter the comparison. Claims are limited on purpose. The Portuguese home test (64% woke more easily, 71% kept using it) had no control group and was run in Portugal [S1], so it should not be used as proof of effect in Spain. Medical certification is highlighted for Philips and Lumie, and Lumora has no such claim [S7]. Competitor warranty and repairability are unknown, so the 2-year warranty and replaceable parts are stated as Lumora facts, without comparison. The seasonal argument (dark mornings until about 8:30) is unverified and is not used. The seasonal clock-change debate is unresolved, so the message stays on "dark winter mornings". Launching in October 2026, before winter, fits the winter-difficulty need [S3]. Assumptions: the final price is 89 euros; the channel mix depends on retailer negotiations; and the marketing budget split is not yet defined.

campaign.concept: "Amaneceres suaves": winter mornings in Spain start in the dark, and Lumora turns that moment into a gentle sunrise in your bedroom. The campaign shows the 30-minute sunrise as a slow, warm, visual ritual, from deep red to daylight white, followed by a soft sound. It rounds off with the evening sunset mode. This expresses the positioning: a full-featured, simple and durable sunrise lamp for people who struggle to get up on dark winter mornings, at around 90 euros. It makes no medical or comparative claims.

key_messages.headline: Amanece en tu habitación. Aunque fuera sea de noche.
key_messages.body: Lumora es la lámpara despertador de luz solar que ilumina tu habitación poco a poco durante 30 minutos, hasta 300 lux, del rojo profundo al blanco luz de día, y termina con un sonido suave. Incluye modo atardecer, 8 sonidos de la naturaleza y radio FM. Se maneja con la app o con los botones físicos. 2 años de garantía y piezas reemplazables. 89 €.

key_messages.headline: Todo lo que buscas en una lámpara despertador, en una sola
key_messages.body: Amanecer gradual de 30 minutos, modo atardecer para acabar el día con calma, 8 sonidos naturales y radio FM. Con app para iOS y Android o sin ella, con botones en la propia lámpara. Diseñada para durar: 2 años de garantía y piezas reemplazables.

key_messages.headline: Lumora. Despertar con luz, sin sobresaltos.
key_messages.body: Una luz que crece durante 30 minutos, hasta 300 lux, y un sonido suave al final. Modo atardecer, 8 sonidos naturales, radio FM, app o botones. 2 años de garantía y piezas reemplazables. Pruébala aquí. 89 €.

key_messages.headline: Un regalo para las mañanas de invierno
key_messages.body: Lumora llena tu mesita de noche de luz de amanecer: del rojo profundo al blanco luz de día, durante 30 minutos. Por la noche, su modo atardecer te acompaña al final del día. Fácil de usar, con app o con botones, y pensada para durar: 2 años de garantía y piezas reemplazables.

key_messages.headline: Las mañanas oscuras ya no tienen que empezar de golpe
key_messages.body: Descubre Lumora: amanecer gradual de 30 minutos hasta 300 lux, modo atardecer, 8 sonidos de la naturaleza y radio FM. Funciona con la app o con botones físicos. Garantía de 2 años y piezas reemplazables, porque está hecha para repararse, no para tirarse. Envío a toda España. 89 €.

key_messages.headline: Lumora: lámpara despertador de amanecer diseñada en Portugal
key_messages.body: Creada por Claridade, empresa de Oporto fundada en 2019, Lumora ofrece un amanecer simulado de 30 minutos (hasta 300 lux, del rojo profundo al blanco luz de día), modo atardecer, 8 sonidos naturales, radio FM, app para iOS y Android y botones físicos. Incluye 2 años de garantía y diseño reparable con piezas reemplazables. Precio de lanzamiento en España: 89 €. Disponemos de unidades para prueba.

content_ideas: Amazon.es listing with A+ content: a 30-minute sunrise timeline graphic (deep red to daylight white), a feature grid (300 lux, sunset mode, 8 sounds, FM radio) and a short video of the lamp running in a dark bedroom.
Own online shop launch landing page in Spanish with a 'sunrise simulator' animation, an app-or-buttons explainer and a repair and replaceable parts section.
In-store demo display for the national electronics chain: a dimmed 'dark morning' bedside corner where the lamp runs its sunrise, with shelf cards listing the key features and the 2-year warranty.
Department store gift-season display for the winter period, with a bedside set-up and a clear price tag at 89 euros, and no discount promotions.
Review seeding kit for Spanish product review media: a lamp, a factual spec sheet and a repairability guide, with an offer of a call with the Portuguese designers.
Short vertical videos for the Amazon.es listing and the online shop: 'A winter morning in 30 minutes', filmed from first red glow to daylight white.
Own online shop email series for first-time visitors and buyers: set-up tips, how to use sunset mode, and how to order spare parts.
Printed quick-start card in the box and short how-to videos that show the app and the physical buttons, for users who prefer no app.
campaign.visual_direction: Calm, warm and modern. Palette built on the sunrise gradient: deep red, amber and soft orange fading into daylight white, set against a dark night-blue and charcoal for the 'before dawn' scenes. Photography of real Spanish bedrooms in winter pre-dawn, with the lamp on a bedside table and light slowly filling the room; natural textures such as linen, wood and wool. Clean, rounded product shots that show the lamp's design and its physical buttons. Light, spacious typography with a gentle sans-serif and plenty of white space. Simple icons for 30 minutes, 300 lux, sunset, sounds, FM and warranty. Packaging should be minimal and sunrise-gradient accented, with a visible 2-year warranty mark and a QR code to the repair and spare parts page. No medical imagery, no before/after body or sleep visuals, no competitor references.

issues.message: This need rests on S16, a foreign-language blog (optimizeyourbiology.com) that reviews the Lumie range, apparently outside Spain. It is not a Spanish consumer source, and the analysis does not mark it as weak or foreign. Back the need with Spanish sources, or flag it in data_quality_notes as weak and not specific to Spain. The Lumie feature details also lean on the UK lumie.com site (S11) with no note that its models or prices may differ in Spain. Evidence: analysis.customer_needs = "Control over sunrise duration and brightness; reviewers criticised limited brightness options and having to re-enable the alarm every day [S16]"

This is listed as a customer need, but no source shows that Spanish buyers want it. Only one article, which may carry affiliate links, mentions certification of the competitors. data_quality_notes admits the claim 'comes from one article'. The need should be presented as a competitor attribute reported by a single weak source, not as a demonstrated need of the target segments. Evidence: analysis.customer_needs = "Medical certification, which is highlighted for Philips and Lumie in review coverage [S7]"

The positioning states as fact that Lumora is clearly cheaper than Philips. The analysis flags a conflict between Philips web prices (142 to 282 euros) and the document's 60-200 euro range, and the pricing_direction says the "below Philips" position is an assumption. Philips also starts at 60 euros in the document, which is below 89. No reliable Lumie price exists. Remove or soften the price comparison in the positioning until Philips and Lumie prices have been compared on the Spanish market. Evidence: strategy.positioning_statement = "at a clearly lower price than Philips' indicative web prices"

The headline features (300 lux, natural sounds, FM radio, sunset mode) are already offered by Philips HF3531 (300 lux, 7 sounds, FM radio) and Lumie Shine 300 (FM radio, 14 sounds), according to the analysis. Lumie Glow 150 has 10 sounds, so 8 sounds is not a distinct feature either. The real differences are the app plus physical buttons, the less bulky design, the repairable design and the 2-year warranty. Competitor warranty and repairability are unknown. Build the value proposition on those points, and on a verified price gap if one is confirmed, instead of on a feature checklist the competitors already match. Evidence: strategy.value_proposition = "You get the features buyers look for (300 lux, sounds, FM radio, sunset mode) at around 90 euros."
